Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - Acme Corp

Hi Sofia 

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated for Acme:

- Monthly token volume: you mentioned this quarters forecast would be around ~200M tokens/month  can you confirm whether that is consumed as a single workload or split across a few product flows?
- Budget target: you said leadership wants to keep unit economics near $/1M tokens in the low-to-mid 3 digits. Can you share a target range (e.g. $700-$900 per 1M tokens) or a hard budget cap?
- GPU preference: you flagged A100 as familiar, but were open to H100 if it materially improves perf/cost. Any hard requirements?
- Throughput targets: we need concurrent sessions, average completion length, and latency SLOs. If you can provide avg response tokens and target p95 latency for a 256512 token completion that helps.

Attached is the usage sheet you shared on the call  I filled in a couple of assumptions where things were fuzzy. When you confirm the bullets above Ill sketch 2 reserved capacity options (cost-first and latency-first) with approximate $/1M token numbers.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the numbers above by EOD tomorrow
- Well send a short pricing comparison and suggest a capacity recommendation + recommended GPU types
- Book a 30-min pricing review next week if helpful

[Attachment: acme_initial_usage_estimates.csv (CSV, 42KB)]

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - Acme Corp

Hi Marcus 

Good recap. See answers below:

- Token volumes: confirmed ~200M tokens/month. It's primarily our chat assistant workload (85%) + smaller batch reranking tasks (15%).
- Budget & unit economics: leadership is targeting roughly $700	300 per 1M tokens for the reserved setup. Our procurement team will look for an overall committed spend of ~ $20k/month initially (flex to grow next quarter).
- GPU preference: our infra team prefers A100 (we've benchmarked there), but we are open to H100 if Redwood can demonstrate meaningful savings or latency improvements.
- Throughput / latency: average completion ~400 tokens, peak concurrent sessions ~50, 95th latency target is <500ms for a 256-token response (we can accept higher for 512-token completions). For throughput planning assume 80 concurrent in peaks across regions.

We'd appreciate two options from you:
1) Cost-optimized reserved capacity that meets the $700	300 / 1M tokens goal
2) Latency-optimized config (p95 < 500ms) and the incremental cost impact

Happy to book a follow-up pricing call  mornings (PST) next Tue/Wed work.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Product Ops, Acme Corp
sofia@acme.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - Acme Corp

Sofia 

Perfect, thanks for the details. Based on your answers I sketched two high-level Dedicated configurations (very rough numbers, will refine if you share actual token shape distributions):

Option A  Cost-optimized:
- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA A100 (80GB) reserved pool
- Expected throughput: ~2.5	3.0M tokens/hour per GPU at typical batch sizes and caching
- Estimated unit cost: ~$750 per 1M tokens (falls in your target range)
- Notes: Good fit if you want to hit the $/1M target with predictable monthly spend.

Option B  Latency-optimized:
- Hardware: 4x NVIDIA H100 (80GB) reserved pool + 2x A100 for background batch workloads
- Expected throughput: higher peak throughput and significantly lower p95 for short completions
- Estimated unit cost: ~$950	3$1,100 per 1M tokens (depends on batching and model choice)
- Notes: Better for strict p95 latency < 500ms and bursty traffic; higher unit cost but fewer instances may be needed for very low latency.

Sizing assumptions used: average completion 400 tokens, peak concurrent 80 sessions, we assumed continuous usage smoothing and prefix caching for chats. If you expect very spiky traffic we recommend additional hot standby GPUs.

Next steps I suggest:
- Confirm which option to validate further (A or B)
- If A, confirm we should price to meet $20k/month committed spend and we’ll map to reserved GPU count+monthly price
- If B, we’ll run a quick perf estimate and provide a p95 latency projection with 95% confidence intervals

I’ve attached a PDF with line-item assumptions and a quick cost model for 4	12 GPU configs. Happy to walk through on a call.

[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf (PDF, 128KB)]

Thanks,
Marcus
